newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rights group wants exhumation of rebel girls.
newsitem.headline: Peru rights group wants exhumation of rebel girls.

text.p: A Peruvian human rights group called Saturday for the bodies of two teenage rebel girls, killed in the raid on the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, to be exhumed so that they can be properly identified.

"We are trying to find out where the two girls' bodies were buried to open the two tombs to identify them," Miguel Jugo, sub-director of the Human Rights Association (APRODEH) told Radioprogramas radio.
All 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas were killed in Tuesday's military assault that secured the rescue of all but one of the 72 hostages held in the residence for 126 days.

The guerrillas' bodies were hurriedly buried by authorities in cemeteries scattered throughout Lima on Thursday night. In many cases, relatives were not allowed to see the bodies beforehand and were only informed subsequently of where they had been buried.

In his first interview since the end of the hostage crisis, President Alberto Fujimori told Reuters on Friday that the rebels' bodies had been placed in clearly marked graves. "If there are any relatives that wish to recover the bodies, there is still time for them to do so," he said.
Many of the rebels were teenagers from Peru's eastern jungle region, recruited into the movement at a young age.
